 Tech Microsoft stock jumps 5% as cloud growth drives earnings and revenue beat
 Published Wed, Oct 28 2026 12:00 PM EDT Updated 1 Min Ago Jordan Novet @in/jordannovet/ WATCH LIVE Key Points Microsoft reported 19% revenue growth, topping estimates.
 Azure cloud revenue jumped 48% to $33.2 billion.
 Free cash flow declined 27% from a year ago.
 In this article
 MSFT 
 Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella speaks at a company event at La Defense business district in Puteaux, near Paris, on Oct. 20, 2026. Dimitar Dilkoff | AFP | Getty Images Microsoft shares rose 5% in extended trading on Wednesday after the software maker reported fiscal first-quarter results that came in stronger than analysts had expected.
 Here's how the company fared relative to LSEG consensus:
 Earnings per share: $4.89 adjusted vs. $4.73 expected
 Revenue: $92.28 billion vs. $90.69 billion expected
 Microsoft's revenue grew 19% year over year in the quarter, which ended on Sept. 30, according to a statement . 
 Net income of $36.63 billion, or $4.92 per share, increased from $27.75 billion, or $3.72 per share, in the same quarter of last year. Adjusted earnings exclude a roughly $200 million impact from investing in OpenAI.
 Free cash flow of $18.63 billion moved 27% lower. Cloud rival Alphabet showed negative free cash flow for the quarter, while Meta said last week that it went free cash flow negative .
 Microsoft has been rapidly building out data center infrastructure to accommodate artificial intelligence demand. The company had $45.2 billion worth of capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter, up about 30%. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount had projected $50.67 billion.
 For the first time in an earnings statement, Microsoft disclosed revenue from its Azure cloud in dollars, at $33.17 billion in the quarter, up 48%. Analysts polled by StreetAccount had expected $32.32 billion, which would have represented growth of more than 44%. The growth rate in the June quarter was 42%.
 Microsoft reported results under two operating segments for the first time since 1998. For the past 11 years it had three segments that divided up its Azure, Office and Windows businesses.
 This story is developing. Please check back for updates.
